clue.text: Possible result of a drop in holiday time

parts.note: a break is a short holiday
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Something that might happen when you take a short holiday, as if a drop in time off had consequences.
explanation.definitionFit: When something fragile is dropped, damage of this kind is a likely outcome, so the definition describes it by its cause.

clue.text: Some Greek characters wanting others beheaded

indicators.note: a beheaded word loses its first letter, so the opening letter of the other Greek characters goes

parts.note: other Greek characters, here betas, the second letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A grisly scene: some Greeks want others to lose their heads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greek characters' reads as people but means letters of the alphabet; the other letters are betas, which 'beheaded' strips of their first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The seventh letter of the Greek alphabet in the plural is a set of Greek characters.

clue.text: Sense in which "Señora" would be incorrect

indicators.note: letters arranged incorrectly are put in a different order, so this signals rearranging the Spanish title

parts.note: the Spanish title, its letters taken as written with the tilde ignored

explanation.surface: A remark on when it would be wrong to address someone as Señora.
explanation.definitionFit: Reason and sense are synonyms for sound judgement or rationality, as in 'see sense'.

clue.text: No longer means to buy wife a male Manx cat

parts.note: a as written, followed by M, the abbreviation for male

indicators.note: a Manx cat has no tail, so the word for the cat loses its last letter

parts.note: a puma is a big cat

explanation.surface: An odd purchase: buying your wife a male Manx cat as a gift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Manx cat' looks like one breed; 'Manx' is the instruction to dock the tail of PUMA, giving PUM.
explanation.definitionFit: Wampum, strings of shell beads, served Native Americans as currency, an obsolete means of payment.

clue.text: Sports facilities providing very cold beverages, but no large cups

indicators.note: means the letters for the large cups are left out of the beverages

parts.note: iced drinks are very cold beverages
DD is a large bra cup size

explanation.surface: A sports venue serving chilled drinks but without big cups to drink them from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cups' suggests drinking vessels, but DD is a bra cup size, removed from ICED DRINKS.
explanation.definitionFit: Ice rinks are venues for skating and ice hockey, so they count as sports facilities.

clue.text: Twice caught one flirting with master artisan

indicators.note: flirting suggests playing about, so the letters are toyed with and rearranged together with the word master
says the pair of letters for caught and one is written two times over

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone twice caught flirting with their master craftsman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twice caught one' gives CICI; 'flirting with' then mixes CICI with MASTER. 'master artisan' tempts as one definition, but 'master' is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A ceramicist is a potter, a craftsperson working in clay, so an artisan.

clue.text: Raised female wildebeest in this country, as a form of self-defence

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the whole construction is read upwards, backwards
puts the female and wildebeest letters inside the country's letters

parts.note: UK, the United Kingdom, from a British setter's viewpoint
a gnu is a wildebeest

explanation.surface: A female wildebeest raised in Britain learning to defend herself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raised' only works because this is a down entry, where reading upwards turns the whole container backwards; 'this country' is the UK from the British setter's point of view.
explanation.definitionFit: Kung fu is a Chinese martial art, used for unarmed combat and protection.

clue.text: Reddening of skin due to very thematic content

indicators.note: the contents of the phrase are the letters inside it, so the answer is concealed within very thematic

explanation.surface: A dermatologist's diagnosis blaming a rash on overly thematic subject matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'content' reads as subject matter but signals that the answer sits inside 'very thematic'.
explanation.definitionFit: Erythema is the medical term for redness of the skin caused by inflamed capillaries.

clue.text: Innocent-looking child sat in front of Polish revolutionary

indicators.note: places the revolutionary's letters before those for polish

parts.note: Che Guevara, the Argentine-born Marxist revolutionary
to rub is to polish

explanation.surface: A sweet-faced child seated before a revolutionary from Poland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' looks like a nationality but is the verb meaning to rub.
explanation.definitionFit: A cherub, a winged angel-child in art, describes a chubby, angelic-looking youngster.

clue.text: Article about a southern Irish town

indicators.note: turns the article round so it reads backwards

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A newspaper article about a town in the south of Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'southern Irish' looks like one description, but 'southern' gives S and 'Irish town' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Naas is the county town of Kildare in the Republic of Ireland.

clue.text: Merchant ship's officer has high-performance vehicle to run

parts.note: a supercar is a very fast, expensive sports car
to go is to run, as a machine runs

explanation.surface: A ship's officer owns a fast sports car to get around in.
explanation.definitionFit: A supercargo is the officer on a trading vessel who manages the cargo and its sale.

clue.text: Land beside house in German forest

parts.note: Arden is the forest in Shakespeare's As You Like It and in Warwickshire, England

explanation.surface: A plot of ground next to a home somewhere in a German forest.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden is the cultivated plot attached to a home, so the land by the house.

clue.text: Pie contaminated with dirt leads to angry hotel's hurried complaint

indicators.note: contaminated things are spoiled and mixed up, so the letters of pie, dirt and the leading letters are jumbled
the leads of words are their first letters, here of angry, hotel's and hurried

explanation.surface: A dirty pie causes an angry hotel guest to complain hastily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complaint' suggests a grumble about the food, but it is an illness. The A, H, H from 'leads to' join PIE and DIRT in the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: Diphtheria is a serious bacterial infection, and complaint is a word for an ailment or disease.

clue.text: Address of Rue Simon's building?

indicators.note: building suggests construction, so these letters are assembled into a new word

parts.note: the letters of Rue Simon, a made-up Paris street

explanation.surface: Asking where a building on the Rue Simon is located.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Address' looks like a street location but is a form of address, a title.
explanation.definitionFit: Monsieur is the French courtesy title for a man, a polite way of addressing him.

clue.text: Springtime by the end of February, unusually

definitions.text: Springtime by the end of February, unusually

parts.words: Springtime by the end of February, unusually
parts.note: read as a jump plus a time, coming at the close of February only in some years

explanation.surface: Spring arriving unusually early, before February is out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Springtime' reads as the season but splits as a jump and a period of 24 hours, which comes at February's end only every fourth year.
explanation.definitionFit: The 29th of February is added only in certain years, so it falls at the month's end unusually.

clue.text: Relating to chain of islands where male carries étui around

indicators.note: the man's name holds the rearranged letters inside it

parts.note: Alan is a man's name

indicators.note: means the letters of the case are moved around into a new order

parts.note: an étui is a small ornamental case for needles

explanation.surface: On an island chain, a man carries a little needle case about with him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' looks like a containment signal, but the containing is done by 'carries'; 'around' rearranges the case's letters to EUTI.
explanation.definitionFit: The Aleutian Islands are an archipelago stretching west from Alaska, and the adjective describes them.

clue.text: Hoped to get answer, like some churches?

parts.note: spired means having a steeple, as many churches do

explanation.surface: Praying for an answer, as people in churches might.
explanation.definitionFit: To aspire is to hope or aim for something, so the past tense matches hoped.

clue.text: Internal organs of ten different birds

indicators.note: a different form of the word ten is its letters reordered

parts.note: rails are marsh birds such as the water rail

explanation.surface: A dissection showing the internal organs of ten unlike birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Entrails are the intestines and other innards of a body, the viscera.

clue.text: Mishandle a tiller, sadly leading to end of boat

indicators.note: puts the rearranged letters before the final letter
sadly here means badly or poorly done, so the letters of a tiller are messed up
the end of a word is its last letter, taken from boat

explanation.surface: Steering a boat badly with its tiller, ending up with the vessel damaged.
explanation.definitionFit: To ill-treat is to treat cruelly or roughly, so to handle someone badly.

clue.text: Second coffee? Third of morning

parts.note: a latte is a milky coffee

indicators.note: picks the third letter of the word morning

explanation.surface: Ordering a second coffee, the third of the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second' looks like a second cup, but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The latter of two things is the one mentioned second, as opposed to the former.

clue.text: Going to bed, leaving note: "Getting sleepy"

indicators.note: means the note departs, taken out of the word for going to bed

parts.note: retiring means going to bed for the night
re is the second note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Someone heading off to bed leaves a message saying they are drowsy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'note' suggests a written message, but it is the musical note RE.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiring means becoming weary, the state of growing tired and ready to sleep.

clue.text: Change from GMT, when in China

indicators.note: puts the time letters inside the slang word for friend

parts.note: china is rhyming slang for mate, from china plate
UT, Universal Time, is the modern name for Greenwich Mean Time

explanation.surface: Adjusting your watch from Greenwich time when you arrive in China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like the country, but in Cockney rhyming slang 'china plate' means mate, a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: To mutate is to change form or undergo alteration, as genes do.

clue.text: Old woman with comic role as 14's other half?

indicators.note: with means alongside, so the old woman's letters are joined directly to the comic role's

parts.note: ma is mother, informally one's old woman
the dame is the comic female part in British pantomime, played by a man

explanation.surface: An elderly woman cast in a comic part as somebody's partner.
explanation.walkthrough: The dame in a British Christmas pantomime is a comic woman's role traditionally played by a man; the definition points to 14-across, whose French female counterpart this is.
explanation.definitionFit: The French title for a married woman pairs with the title for a man, so it is his other half.

clue.text: Another setter was in tears after newspaper lost acceptance amongst the young and hip?

definitions.text: acceptance amongst the young and hip?

indicators.note: another version of the word setter is its letters in a fresh order
means the newspaper's letter is lost from the word for weeping

parts.note: cried means was in tears
i is the British newspaper, sister paper of the Independent

explanation.surface: A rival crossword setter wept after their paper dropped them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Another' rearranges SETTER to STREET; CRIED loses I, the British daily newspaper called i, to give CRED.
explanation.definitionFit: Street cred is credibility or standing among fashionable young people, informal slang.

clue.text: Band's first organ stand

indicators.note: takes the first letter of Band's, its opening letter

parts.note: the ear is the organ of hearing

explanation.surface: A group's debut organ being put on its stand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organ' suggests the instrument, but it is a body organ.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear is to stand or tolerate, as in 'I can't bear it'.

clue.text: Sticky seedcase found in 50% of Mexican dishes

indicators.note: takes half the letters, the front half, of the word for these dishes

parts.note: burritos are Mexican tortilla wraps

explanation.surface: A clingy seed pod found in half of the Mexican food on the table.
explanation.definitionFit: A burr is a prickly seed head that clings to fur and clothing.

clue.text: Exodus of the giraffes

indicators.note: means the answer is made of letters taken out of the giraffes, sitting inside those words

explanation.surface: A mass departure of giraffes, a wildlife migration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exodus' points to a Bible book, but here it is a flight.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hegira was Muhammad's flight from Mecca, and by extension any mass departure.

clue.text: Man rules out 8 and 13, say

indicators.note: out here means wrong or disordered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man rules certain clues out of contention.
explanation.walkthrough: '8 and 13' look like references to other clues, but they are simply examples of figures.
explanation.definitionFit: Eight and thirteen are examples of numbers, written in figures.
